postmortem.assessment: The thesis needed a benign CPI and falling oil, and both went the other way within two sessions. The Opposition named exactly these risks (core at 0.3%, hike pricing with room to rise, repeated failures of US-Iran peace hopes, and a stop inside one month's normal range), and Janus's own probability after reading it was 50%, so the position expressed no view and existed only to meet C06's two-position floor. Taking a coin-flip long into a scheduled CPI release with a 17bp stop was a poor decision whatever the outcome; the size of the oil move on 12 November was bad luck, but the direction of the CPI risk was flagged in advance. The loss was contained because the size was the minimum.
postmortem.do_differently: 1. Do not open a position at a 50% probability to satisfy a count rule: C07 and then C08 already removed this, and the forecast record should lean to the side the evidence favours (here, The Opposition's side) rather than sit at even. 2. When The Opposition's case rests on a scheduled release inside the first days of the window, weight it more heavily in p_final. 3. Treat oil-driven rallies in long yields as fragile while Hormuz shipping is still being attacked.
